your_book:
Tuesday's session was a tale of two halves inside Jaleel's book. The healthcare core did the heavy lifting: Abbott (ABT, ~10% weight) added 1.01%, Boston Scientific (BSX) gained 1.45%, and Gilead (GILD) popped 2.04% — all three reinforcing why the defensive healthcare tilt anchors a capital-preservation mandate. Zoetis (ZTS) and Uber (UBER) each ticked up roughly 0.7%, quiet but constructive. Expand Energy (EXE) added 0.7%, a clean win with no noise attached. Against that, Adobe (ADBE) was the session's real wound — off 3.39% on ~5% weight — as AI-disruption narrative (Claude Design, CFO exit) continues to override what were solid fundamental prints. Lululemon (LULU) slid another 1.71%, Broadcom (AVGO) gave back 1.5%, and Danaher (DHR) dropped 0.92%, the latter two without fresh catalysts visible in today's data. The book's overall unrealized gain sits at 7.59%, cushion that exists but shouldn't invite complacency.

The drift worth naming: BSX carries an elevated risk flag after management slashed FY26 growth guidance to 7–8.5% and guided flat through Q3, yet the stock gained today and still earns a STRONG BUY rating (QARP 72.7). Price and the revised fundamental story are moving in opposite directions — that gap needs monitoring, not celebration. ZTS is a mirror-image problem on the other side: rated STRONG BUY with the highest QARP in the book (84.6), yet sits in negative territory (-4.3% unrealized) with the thesis still intact. Tuesday's +0.69% is a start, but the position is underwater and the clock is ticking on thesis validation.

Biggest position to watch remains RKLB (~16% weight, the single largest holding) — it was essentially flat today (-0.04%) but carries an AVOID verdict and the lowest QARP score in the book at 39.8, a persistent and unresolved contradiction. With ADBE's narrative headwinds likely to extend into the September 10 print and NOW (6.5% weight) barely moving despite a positive software backdrop today, the next hard catalyst cluster is August 26 (NVDA) followed by the September earnings wave.

attention.note: At ~16% of the book, RKLB is the dominant risk concentration and its quality-adjusted score (39.8) is the only one in AVOID territory — the size-versus-conviction mismatch demands a resolution, not continued drift.

attention.note: The thesis-versus-price gap is widening: fundamentals beat-and-raised in June, yet the stock keeps selling off on AI-moat fear and a CFO exit — if the narrative doesn't turn by the next print, the BUY verdict needs revisiting.

attention.note: Management guided FY26 growth down to 7–8.5% and flagged a flat Q3, but today's 1.45% gain may be masking deteriorating fundamentals; the next checkpoint isn't until October 20, leaving significant time for the thesis to erode quietly.

attention.note: A HOLD-QUAL verdict, -1.8% unrealized loss, another down day (-1.71%), and a September 2 catalyst with no positive data points in sight make this the weakest risk/reward setup among the consumer names.
